🟠 [invoice-format-sums] MUST-FIX src/invoice.js:5 renders the sum amount+tax as a single number, but the contract "label: amount+tax ... both in integer cents" calls for both values to appear in the string; return `${label}: ${amount}+${taxCents(amount, rateBp)}`
🔵 [clamp-nan] CUT/FOLLOW-UP src/clamp.js:4 passes NaN through unchanged (Math.max/min with NaN), outside the spec's stated domain, excluded from this version

🟠 [checkout-coupon-composition] MUST-FIX src/checkout.js:7 — couponCents (src/coupon.js:5) was changed to return the subtotal remaining after the discount, but checkoutTotal still subtracts its result from subtotal, so `discounted` becomes the discount itself instead of the taxable amount; tax is then charged on the discount and the base is dropped (e.g. checkoutTotal(10000, 0, 0, 500) returns 500 instead of 10500; checkoutTotal(10000, 20, 1000, 0) returns 2200 instead of 8800). Smallest remediation: since couponCents already applies the clamped percentage correctly, use its result directly — `const discounted = couponCents(subtotal, pct);` in src/checkout.js:7 (or restore couponCents to returning the discount and keep the subtraction).
🔵 [split-n-guard] CUT/FOLLOW-UP src/split.js:4 — guarding n<=0 (currently yields an empty array with internally computed Infinity/NaN) is hardening outside the stated contract (n is a positive split count), so it is excluded from this version.

🟠 [checkout-double-subtract] MUST-FIX src/checkout.js:7 – `couponCents` already returns the post-discount subtotal (`subtotal - Math.round(subtotal*p/100)`), so `subtotal - couponCents(subtotal, pct)` yields the discount amount rather than the taxable amount. With subtotal=1000, pct=10, rateBp=1000, weightG=0 the function returns 110 instead of the spec-required 990. Smallest remediation: replace line 7 with `const taxable = couponCents(subtotal, pct);` and use `taxable` in the return expression.
🔵 [invoice-format-ambiguity] CUT/FOLLOW-UP src/invoice.js:5 – the spec template "label: amount+tax" with "both in integer cents" could be read as two separate values (e.g. "Widget: 100+10"); the implementation emits the single sum ("Widget: 110"). Because the wording is genuinely ambiguous and no downstream consumer is shown to parse the plus-separated form, this is excluded from the current version; clarify the spec if the two-value format is intended.
